cli.usage:
Usage: adlc <command> [--json]
  adlc help [topic|command]   (guides and every command with an example; adlc <command> --help too)
  adlc --version   (the platform version)
  Through the API (needs adlc login, or SDLC_API_URL and SDLC_API_TOKEN in CI):
    adlc login [--api-url <https://...>] [--token-stdin]
    adlc logout
    adlc whoami
    adlc intent create|list|show …   (run adlc intent for details)
    adlc next <INT-…>   (where the intent is and what you do next)
    adlc doctor   (check your login and the API, and what to fix; changes nothing)
    adlc gate approve|reject|request-changes <G> <INT-…> …   (run adlc gate for details)
    adlc escalation list|show|ack|decide …   (run adlc escalation for details)
    adlc ai-record show|set …   (run adlc ai-record for details)
    adlc spec link|list <INT-…> …   (run adlc spec for details)
    adlc plan submit|list|show|draft <INT-…> …   (draft: a plan file draft on your machine; run adlc plan for details)
    adlc run list <INT-…>, adlc run kill <run ID|INT-…>   (the kill switch; run adlc run for details)
    adlc cost report …   (run adlc cost for details)
    adlc metrics gates …   (gate waiting times; run adlc metrics for details)
    adlc eval plan|run|list|show …   (evaluation plans of a project; run adlc eval for details)
    adlc trial report …   (the community trial's anonymous report, TRIAL.md; run adlc trial for details)
    adlc evidence build|list|show|export <INT-…> …   (Evidence Packs; run adlc evidence for details)
    adlc client request-data-deletion|cancel-data-deletion|status …   (run adlc client for details)
    adlc token create|list|revoke …   (your own API tokens; run adlc token for details)
    adlc admin project|user|identity|passkey|role|config|tenant-admin|token|agent|tool|evidence …   (admins; run adlc admin for details)
    adlc audit verify   (tenant admins)
  Operator commands on the server (need SDLC_DB_URL, application role platform_app):
    adlc ops …   (run adlc ops for details)

adlc: the command line of the Agentic SDLC platform.

  getting-started   log in, find your work, the first intent
  roles             Person A, Person B, the two-person rule
  gates             G1–G8: what each gate needs and who decides

  login, logout, whoami, doctor, intent, next, gate, spec, plan, run, escalation,

cli.help.topic.getting_started:
Getting started
  1. Log in with your personal API token: adlc login --api-url https://<platform>  (the token is asked without showing it).
  2. Check the login and the connection: adlc doctor
  3. See your roles per project: adlc whoami
  4. Create an intent and link its spec: adlc intent create --project <slug> --title <text> --risk low --data-class internal --spec docs/specs/<file>.md
  5. Ask what to do next at any time: adlc next <INT-…>
The user guide (platform/USER-GUIDE.md) walks through a whole intent.
cli.help.topic.roles:
Roles and the two-person rule
  Person A owns the intent: creates it, links the spec, approves G1 (and G2 at Low and Medium risk).
  Person B reviews independently: approves G3, G7 and G8, and G2 at High risk or above.
  The second approver adds a second approval at G7 for flagged changes and at Critical risk.
  Governance and admin handle escalations, exceptions and the project's settings.
  The producer of a change never approves it: whoever submitted a plan never approves G3, and the creator of an intent never approves G7 or G8.
  Your roles per project: adlc whoami. Who an intent waits for: adlc next <INT-…>.
cli.help.topic.gates:
The gates
  G1 intent and risk: Person A approves. The project needs an AI record that allows the data class.
  G2 specification: the linked spec needs acceptance criteria.
  G3 plan: a plan file .sdlc/plans/<INT-…>.yaml on the default branch, submitted with adlc plan submit.
  G4 execution boundary: checked by the platform (Person A approves at High risk); then the agent runs.
  G5 scope and budget: the platform checks the run's changes against the plan and the budget.
  G6 verification: CI of the pull request and security findings.
  G7 review and merge: Person B approves the pull request on GitHub, a person merges it (never the platform).
  G8 release: Person B approves the release; the evidence pack is sealed.
  Low risk passes G2 and G3 without a person when the conditions hold; a person can still block within the block window.
  Where an intent is and what it waits for: adlc next <INT-…>.
cli.help.topic.comments:
Commands in GitHub comments (on the intent's issue or pull request, first line of a new comment)
  /approve G<n>                                   approve a gate (not G7: approve the pull request instead)
  /reject G<n> [reason_code] <reason>             reject a gate
  /request-changes G<n> [reason_code] <reason>    ask for changes
  /ack [ESC-…]                                    acknowledge an escalation
  /decide [ESC-…] <resume|modify|roll-back|terminate|escalate> [reason_code] [reason]
  /kill                                           stop the intent's current run
Your GitHub account must be linked to your platform user (by its numeric account ID). The platform replies only when it refuses a command.
cli.help.topic.troubleshooting:
Troubleshooting
  A command fails to connect, or with a certificate error: run adlc doctor; for a company CA set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.
  Exit code 4 (log in again): your token expired or was revoked; run adlc login.
  Refused with 403: you need a role for this on the project; adlc whoami shows yours, a tenant admin grants them.
  Refused with 404: check the project slug or the intent code; adlc intent list shows yours.
  Refused with 409: the intent moved on; adlc next <INT-…> shows where it is now.
  An intent does not move: adlc next <INT-…> shows what it waits for and why.
  The platform answers 503: a service it needs is not ready; ask the operator to run pnpm doctor.

cli.login.usage:
Usage: adlc login [--api-url <https://...>] [--token-stdin] [--json]
  Asks for your personal API token (sdlc_pat_…) without showing it, or reads it from standard input with --token-stdin. Never put the token on the command line. --api-url is needed the first time; http:// is accepted only for this machine (127.0.0.1, localhost).
cli.login.url_required: Give the API address with --api-url, for example --api-url https://sdlc.example.internal.
cli.login.no_terminal: Standard input is not a terminal. Pipe the token in with --token-stdin; never put it on the command line.
cli.login.stdin_is_terminal: --token-stdin reads a pipe, not the terminal: typing there would show the token. Run adlc login without --token-stdin to get a hidden prompt.
cli.login.token_invalid: This is not a personal API token: it must start with sdlc_pat_ and have 52 characters. Nothing was saved.
cli.login.aborted: The input was cancelled or too long. Nothing was saved.
cli.login.done: Logged in as {name} <{email}> in tenant {tenant} at {api_url}. The token is saved in {path} (readable only by you).
cli.login.env_overrides: Note: SDLC_API_TOKEN is set in this shell, so commands use it instead of the saved login.
cli.logout.done: The token is revoked on the server and the saved login is deleted on this machine.
cli.logout.not_revoked: The saved login is deleted on this machine, but the token could not be revoked on the server: it stays valid until it expires. Revoke it with adlc token revoke from another login, or ask a tenant admin.
cli.logout.none: There is no saved login on this machine.
cli.token.usage:
Usage (your own personal API tokens, through the API):
  adlc token create --name <token-name> [--days <1-365>] [--json]   (the token is shown once)
  adlc token list [--json]
  adlc token revoke --id <token-id> [--json]
cli.token.for_other_user: This token belongs to another person and lasts at most 7 days. Give it to them once, through a safe channel. They must create their own token with adlc token create, then revoke this one with adlc token revoke.
cli.audit.usage: Usage: adlc audit verify [--json]   (tenant admins; the operator's check on the server is adlc ops audit verify)
cli.not_logged_in: You are not logged in. Run adlc login --api-url <address>, or set SDLC_API_URL and SDLC_API_TOKEN (CI only).
cli.env.incomplete: Set both SDLC_API_URL and SDLC_API_TOKEN, or neither (then the saved login of adlc login is used).
cli.env.token_invalid: SDLC_API_TOKEN is not a personal API token (sdlc_pat_…, 52 characters).
cli.tls_disabled: NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 turns off certificate checks. The adlc command never runs without them: unset it, and add your company CA with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS instead.
cli.api_url.invalid: The API address is not a valid http(s) URL.
cli.api_url.insecure: The API address must use https://. http:// is accepted only for this machine (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]).
cli.api_url.credentials: The API address must not contain a user name or password.
cli.api_url.query: The API address must not contain a query (?) or a fragment (#).
cli.credentials.no_config_dir: No folder for the saved login: set HOME or XDG_CONFIG_HOME to an absolute path.
cli.credentials.unsafe_mode: {path} can be read by other users. Run chmod 600 {path}, then log in again: the token may have been read.
cli.credentials.not_a_file: {path} is not a regular file. Delete it and run adlc login again.
cli.credentials.not_owner: {path} belongs to another user. Delete it and run adlc login again.
cli.credentials.malformed: {path} cannot be read. Run adlc login again.
cli.api.http_status: The API answered with HTTP status {status} and no readable error.
cli.api.login_again: Your token is missing, expired or revoked. Get a new one (adlc token create from another login, or ask a tenant admin), then run adlc login.
cli.api.network: The API cannot be reached. Check the address, the network and the certificate (add a company CA with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS).
cli.api.timeout: The API did not answer in time. Try again later.
cli.api.redirect: The API answered with a redirect. The adlc command never follows redirects, so your token is not sent to another address: check the API address.
cli.api.too_large: The API answer is too large. Check the API address.
cli.api.malformed: The API answer has an unexpected format. The API and this adlc command may have different versions.

cli.next.evaluations_none: No evaluation ended in the last 7 days in your projects.
cli.next.evaluation_ended: Evaluation {code} ({project}) ended {finished_at}: {status}. Read the report: adlc eval report {code}
cli.next.advice.decide_gate: Decide {gate}: adlc gate approve {gate} {intent} (or reject, request-changes){comment}.
cli.next.advice.decide_g4: Read the run proposal (adlc intent show {intent}), then decide G4: adlc gate approve G4 {intent} (or reject, request-changes){comment}.
cli.next.advice.decide_g5: Look at the run's changes and cost, then decide G5: adlc gate approve G5 {intent} (or reject, request-changes){comment}.
cli.next.advice.decide_g5_review: The change is too large to review as one piece, or its size is unknown. Split it: adlc gate request-changes G5 {intent} --reason-code review_too_large (back to G3 for a smaller plan). Or allow it with a reason: adlc gate approve G5 {intent} --reason-code generated_change, mechanical_change or cannot_split{comment}.
cli.next.advice.decide_g6: Look at CI and the security findings on pull request #{pr}, then decide G6: adlc gate approve G6 {intent} (or reject, request-changes){comment}.
cli.next.advice.review_g7: Review pull request #{pr} on GitHub: Approve, or Request changes. G7 takes no adlc command; your GitHub review is the decision.
cli.next.advice.merge_g7: The approvals are complete: a reviewer who is not a producer merges pull request #{pr} on GitHub (the platform never merges).
cli.next.advice.decide_g8: Read the Evidence Pack (adlc evidence show {intent}), then decide the release: adlc gate approve G8 {intent} (or reject, request-changes){comment}.
cli.next.advice.already_approved: You approved {gate} already. It waits for {roles}; approvals needed in all: {needed}.
cli.next.advice.waits_role: Nothing for you now: it waits for {roles}.
cli.next.advice.producer: Nothing for you now: it waits for {roles}. You are a producer of this change (you created the intent or allowed its run), so you never decide {gate}.
cli.next.advice.link_spec: Link the spec, a Markdown file on the default branch with acceptance criteria: adlc spec link {intent} --path <docs/specs/….md>.
cli.next.advice.fix_spec: The linked spec cannot be read on the default branch (removed, too large or not Markdown): fix or restore it, then adlc spec link {intent} --path <path>.
cli.next.advice.spec_unclear: The spec has no acceptance criteria: add them (for example a heading "Acceptance criteria" with a list), merge, then adlc spec link {intent} --path <path>.
cli.next.advice.write_plan: Write the plan file .sdlc/plans/{intent}.yaml (a draft: adlc plan draft {intent} --from <tasks file> --tool spec-kit|bmad), merge it to the default branch, then adlc plan submit {intent}.
cli.next.advice.new_plan: The run changed files outside its plan: write a new plan in .sdlc/plans/{intent}.yaml, merge it, then adlc plan submit {intent}.
cli.next.advice.resubmit_plan: The plan file on the default branch is not the submitted plan: check the change, then adlc plan submit {intent}.
cli.next.advice.ai_record: The project AI record must allow the data class {data_class}: adlc ai-record show {project}, then adlc ai-record set … (run adlc ai-record for the options).
cli.next.advice.escalation: An escalation holds this intent: adlc escalation list --intent {intent}, then adlc escalation ack ESC-… and adlc escalation decide ESC-… <resume|modify|roll-back|terminate|escalate> (its owner or backup, never a producer).
cli.next.advice.waits_escalation: An escalation holds this intent; it waits for its owner ({roles}). See it: adlc escalation list --intent {intent}.
cli.next.advice.block_window: The platform passed a HOTL gate; until {until} a holder of that gate's role may still send it back with /reject <G> or /request-changes <G> on issue #{issue}. Otherwise nothing to do: the intent moves on then.
cli.next.advice.run_running: The agent is running. Nothing to do; follow it with adlc run list {intent}. To stop it: adlc run kill {intent}.
cli.next.advice.run_watch: The agent is running. Nothing to do; follow it with adlc run list {intent}.
cli.next.advice.run_pending: The run is about to start. Nothing to do.
cli.next.advice.proposal: The High-risk run left a proposal: save it (adlc evidence proposal {intent} --output <file>), take it forward yourself, then end the intent: adlc gate reject G4 {intent} --reason-ref <https://…>.
cli.next.advice.ci_pending: Waiting for CI on pull request #{pr}. Nothing to do; a failed check starts a new run while retries last.
cli.next.advice.publish_retry: The platform pushes the change and opens the pull request; it tries again by itself. Nothing to do.
cli.next.advice.changes_requested: A reviewer requested changes: a new run with the feedback starts. Nothing to do.
cli.next.advice.setup_ci: Pull request #{pr} has no CI check at all: G6 cannot pass without independent checks. Add CI to the repository, or fix verification.required_checks (handbook Ch.14 §14.10.3). G6 pauses if no check appears.
cli.next.advice.setup_git_host: The platform cannot read the Git host: tell the operator (platform/deploy/README.md, Troubleshooting).
cli.next.advice.setup_evidence: The platform cannot build the Evidence Pack (no evidence store, or it cannot be reached): tell the operator (platform/deploy/README.md, Troubleshooting).
cli.next.advice.setup_later_gate: A part of the platform this gate needs is off (for example the worker's Cost Controller credentials): tell the operator (platform/deploy/README.md, Troubleshooting).
cli.next.advice.setup_agent: G4 refused the run ({cause}): the agent register or the project configuration must be fixed (adlc admin agent show …, adlc admin config show --project {project}).
cli.next.advice.setup_budget: The budget is used up ({cause}): see adlc cost report --intent {intent} and ask the tenant admin.
cli.next.advice.finished: The intent is {status}. Nothing more to do.
cli.next.advice.blocked: The intent is blocked: at Critical risk the agent never runs. Nothing more to do.
cli.next.advice.unknown: No advice for "{reason}" yet: see adlc intent show {intent}.
cli.next.note.g3_submitter: the platform refuses an approval of G3 from the person who submitted the plan.
cli.next.note.default_roles: who may do this comes from the project's access settings; the roles named here are the defaults.
cli.next.note.admin_only: a tenant admin fixes this; the intent is checked again by itself afterwards.

cli.cost.usage:
Usage (the whole tenant: tenant admins; one project or intent: the roles in access.cost_read_roles, by default Person A, Person B, PM / BrSE, governance and admin; never viewer):
  adlc cost report [--project <slug> | --intent <INT-…>] [--from <time>] [--to <time>] [--by project|intent|model|status] [--json]
  Times are UTC: YYYY-MM-DD (00:00 that day) or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ. --from is included, --to is excluded. Default: the current month. At most 366 days.
cli.cost.header: Cost report for {scope}, from {from} to {to} (UTC, the end excluded). Amounts in USD.
cli.cost.empty: No model calls are recorded in this range.
cli.cost.truncated: Only the {max} rows with the largest cost are shown. The total covers every call. Narrow the scope or the range to see the others.
cli.cost.wasted_note: Wasted = tokens and cost of runs that ended failed, cancelled or stopped (budget, scope, time, stalled, killed).
cli.cost.freshness: Spend is copied from the model gateway every few minutes and when each run ends; calls of the last few minutes may not be shown yet. Latest recorded call: {latest_call}. Last record written: {last_recorded}. Runs still in progress (their cost so far is shown): {runs}.
cli.metrics.usage:
Usage (the whole tenant: tenant admins; one project: the roles in access.metrics_read_roles, by default Person A, Person B, the second approver, PM / BrSE, governance and admin; never viewer):
  adlc metrics agents [--project <slug>] [--agent <key>] [--model <name>] [--from <time>] [--to <time>] [--json]  (needs a role in both access.cost_read_roles and access.metrics_read_roles)
  adlc metrics gates [--project <slug>] [--gate G1..G8] [--mode HITL|HOTL|AUDIT|POLICY] [--risk low|medium|high|critical] [--from <time>] [--to <time>] [--json]
  Times are UTC: YYYY-MM-DD (00:00 that day) or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ. --from is included, --to is excluded. Default: the last 30 days. At most 366 days. The range and --mode select the decisions; the intents at the gate now are always counted.
cli.metrics.header: Gate waiting times for {scope}: decisions from {from} to {to} (UTC, the end excluded).
cli.metrics.no_decisions: No person decided at a gate in this range.
cli.metrics.now_header: Platform passes (HOTL, AUDIT) in the range, and intents at the gate at {as_of}:
cli.metrics.truncated: Only the first {max} rows are shown. Narrow the scope with --project or --gate to see the others.
cli.metrics.note: Waiting time = wall-clock time from the moment the intent entered the gate to the person's decision, not working hours. "after changes" = decisions after a request for changes at the same gate; it includes the time the producer spent on the changes. "At the gate now" counts every intent at a gate, also gates that wait for a run or for CI.
cli.metrics.agents_header: Agent efficiency for {scope}: runs created from {from} to {to} (UTC, the end excluded).
cli.metrics.no_runs: No run was created in this range.
cli.metrics.unattributed: Cost of calls that belong to no run (not in the rows): {cost} USD.
cli.metrics.agents_note: Rates leave out runs still in progress. A run's model is the one the platform chose for it at G4; for older runs, the one with the most cost in its records (unknown without records). CI first try, merged and lead time count under the run that made the event. Wasted = cost of runs that failed, were cancelled or stopped. Lead time is wall-clock time from the intent's creation to its close. Lead / estimate = the lead time of the merged intents with a human-effort estimate, as a percentage of their estimated hours (in brackets: how many intents); calendar time, not working hours. Never per person.

eval.report.note: Numbers from the evaluation harness (L02). Resolved = the hidden tests pass and nothing broke. Intervals: 95% bootstrap over tasks. A difference is called only when the intervals do not overlap and McNemar's p < 0.05. Cost is the internal cost of self-hosted models. Never a prompt, task text or code.

The plan file is JSON with the fields of the API (code, data_class, task_set_version, task_ids, runs_per_task, budget_per_run_usd, monthly_cap_usd, trigger, schedule, configurations); a prompt variant is a path on the default branch, never a text. A role in access.eval_roles changes and runs plans.
cli.eval.task.usage:
Usage:
  adlc eval task draft <INT-YYYY-NNNN> --project <slug> --task <id> [--output <file>] [--force] [--json]
  adlc eval task register <id> --project <slug> [--json]
  adlc eval task list --project <slug> [--json]
  adlc eval task approve <task-uuid> --card <sha256> [--json]
  adlc eval task reject <task-uuid> --card <sha256> --reason not_representative|tests_weak|too_large|needs_environment|other [--json]
A task comes from a merged intent: its spec, the commit before the change, and the tests its pull request added or changed, hidden from the agent. `draft` writes the task card .sdlc/eval-tasks/<id>.yaml on this machine; commit it through a pull request, then `register` it. A person with a role in access.eval_roles who did not work on the intent approves or rejects it after the server checked it. The --card value is the card SHA-256 that `list` shows.

comment.reply.syntax_gate_missing: The command needs a gate, for example `/approve G3`.
comment.reply.syntax_gate_invalid: The gate is not valid. Use a gate code from G1 to G8, for example `/approve G3`.
comment.reply.syntax_unexpected_text: `/approve` takes only the gate, for example `/approve G3`. Nothing was recorded. Write other text on the next line, or in another comment.
comment.reply.syntax_reason_missing: `/reject` and `/request-changes` need a reason after the gate: a reason code, a sentence, or both. Nothing was recorded.
comment.reply.syntax_decision_missing: `/decide` needs a decision: resume, modify, roll-back, terminate or escalate. Nothing was recorded.
comment.reply.syntax_decision_invalid: The decision is not valid. Use resume, modify, roll-back, terminate or escalate. Nothing was recorded.
comment.reply.usage:
Commands (on the first line of a new comment):
- `/approve G<n>`
- `/reject G<n> [reason code] <reason>`
- `/request-changes G<n> [reason code] <reason>`

Valid reason codes: {codes}. A reason code other than `other` may stand alone; without a reason code, the platform records `other`. The reason itself stays in this comment; the platform stores only a link to it.
comment.reply.usage_escalation:
Escalation commands (on the first line of a new comment):
- `/ack [ESC-YYYY-NNNN]`
- `/decide [ESC-YYYY-NNNN] <resume|modify|roll-back|terminate|escalate> [reason code] [reason]`

The escalation code may be left out when the intent has only one escalation that is not decided. Valid reason codes: {codes}. The reason stays in this comment; the platform stores only a link to it.
comment.reply.user_not_linked: {gate}: nothing was recorded. Your GitHub account is not linked to an active platform user. Ask the platform admin to link it.
comment.reply.intent_not_linked: {gate}: nothing was recorded. No open intent is linked to this issue or pull request.
comment.reply.intent_ambiguous: {gate}: nothing was recorded. More than one open intent is linked to this issue or pull request. Use the CLI with the intent code instead.
comment.reply.intent_not_found: {gate}: nothing was recorded. You have no role in the project of this intent.
comment.reply.forbidden: {gate}: nothing was recorded. Your role in this project does not allow this action.
comment.reply.gate_not_supported: {gate}: this gate cannot be decided by a comment command. G1, G2 and G3 can, G4 to G6 when they wait for a person or within the block window of a gate the platform passed, G7 (`/reject` or `/request-changes` only) and G8 when it waits for the release approval.
comment.reply.spec_unclear: {gate}: the linked spec has no acceptance criteria, so it cannot be approved. Add them to the spec and link it again.
comment.reply.review_reason_required: {gate}: the change is larger than the project's review limits, or its size is unknown, so an approval needs a reason code: generated_change, mechanical_change or cannot_split. Nothing was recorded. Or request changes to split the plan at G3.
comment.reply.gate_input_missing: {gate}: the gate has nothing to decide on yet. Link a spec before G2, submit a plan before G3.
comment.reply.gate_not_current: {gate}: the intent is not waiting at this gate, so nothing was recorded. The last status comment shows its current gate. A gate the platform passed can still be rejected or sent back until its block window closes; it cannot be approved again.
comment.reply.plan_refused: {gate}: an agent run went outside this plan, so it cannot be approved again and nothing was recorded. Submit a new plan; G3 then waits for your approval (HITL).
comment.reply.g7_use_pr_review: {gate}: approve the pull request with a GitHub review (**Approve**) instead; nothing was recorded. `/reject G7` and `/request-changes G7` are accepted.
comment.reply.project_not_active: {gate}: the project is archived or not active.
comment.reply.config_invalid: {gate}: the stored project configuration is not valid. Ask the platform operator to fix it.
comment.reply.escalation_not_found: {gate}: nothing was recorded. No escalation that is not decided matches this intent. Name the escalation code, for example `/ack ESC-2026-0001`.
comment.reply.escalation_ambiguous: {gate}: nothing was recorded. This intent has more than one escalation that is not decided. Name the escalation code, for example `/ack ESC-2026-0001`.
comment.reply.escalation_forbidden: {gate}: nothing was recorded. Only the owner, the backup owner (once the escalation reached them) or governance may act on this escalation, and never a producer of the change.
comment.reply.escalation_not_open: {gate}: nothing was recorded. The escalation is already decided or closed.
comment.reply.escalation_already_acknowl: {gate}: nothing was recorded. The escalation is already acknowledged. Decide it with `/decide`.
comment.reply.escalation_decision_not_al: {gate}: nothing was recorded. This decision is not allowed here, for example governance cannot escalate further.
comment.reply.kill_forbidden: Not stopped: you do not hold a role that may use the kill switch on this project (config `access.kill_roles`: by default Person A, Person B and governance).
comment.reply.kill_no_active_run: Not stopped: the intent has no run that is queued or under way.
comment.reply.failed: {gate}: the platform could not record this command. Tell the platform operator.
comment.reply.footer: _Automatic reply of the SDLC platform. Successful commands get no reply; the platform posts the gate status when it changes._

intent.status.submitted: **{code}** was submitted and waits at **G1** ({gate_name}). {mentions}: decide with `/approve G1`, `/reject G1 <reason>` or `/request-changes G1 <reason>`.

intent.status.advanced_platform: **{code}**: {previous_gate} was approved by {deciders}. The intent now waits at **{gate}** ({gate_name}), which the platform checks.
intent.status.rejected: **{code}** was rejected at **{gate}** by {deciders} (reason code `{reason}`). The intent is closed.
intent.status.changes_requested: **{code}**: {deciders} requested changes at **{gate}** (reason code `{reason}`). Update the input of the gate, then decide again. {mentions}
intent.status.hotl_passed: **{code}**: the platform passed **{previous_gate}** (HOTL): its conditions hold. The intent now waits at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). {mentions}: until **{window_end}** you can still block {previous_gate} with `/reject {previous_gate} <reason>` or `/request-changes {previous_gate} <reason>`.
intent.status.returned: **{code}**: {deciders} requested changes at **{gate}** within its block window (reason code `{reason}`). The intent went back from {previous_gate} to **{gate}** ({gate_name}). Update the input of the gate; it then passes again or waits for a person. {mentions}
intent.status.ai_record_refused:
**{code}** cannot enter **G1** ({gate_name}) yet: the project AI record check failed (reason code `{reason}`: `ai_record_missing` means the project has no AI record; `data_class_not_allowed` means the record does not allow the intent's data class). {mentions}: create or update the project AI record. The intent continues when the record allows it.

Until the client has answered in writing, client data is handled only as `client_restricted` (handbook Ch.2 Rule 3).
intent.status.g4_refused: **{code}** cannot start its run at **G4** ({gate_name}) yet: a G4 check failed (reason code `{reason}`). {mentions}: fix the cause (the agent register or `run.agent_key`, the agent's instructions file, the project AI record, the approved spec or plan, or the budget). The platform checks G4 again on its own.
intent.status.blocked: **{code}** was blocked at **G4** ({gate_name}) (reason code `{reason}`): its risk tier or data class allows no agent run (autonomy L0). The agent never runs, and the intent is closed. {mentions}
intent.status.run_proposed: **{code}** waits at **G4** ({gate_name}) for approval of its run: agent `{agent}`, base commit `{base_sha}`. {mentions}: decide with `/approve G4`, `/reject G4 <reason>` or `/request-changes G4 <reason>`. A new commit on the default branch or a changed agent makes a new proposal and voids earlier approvals.
intent.status.agent_recertification_due: **{code}**: its run uses agent `{agent}`, whose recertification is overdue (handbook Ch.20 §20.8). The run is not blocked. {mentions}: recertify the agent.
intent.status.run_started: **{code}**: G4 is passed. The platform starts the agent run. {mentions}
intent.status.run_finished: **{code}**: the agent run ended. The intent now waits at **{gate}** ({gate_name}), where the platform checks the file scope and the budget. {mentions}
intent.status.run_failed: **{code}**: the agent run failed or was stopped. The intent is paused until a person decides on the escalation. {mentions}
intent.status.run_killed: **{code}**: the agent run was stopped with the kill switch. The platform stops the sandbox and revokes the run's keys and tokens; an escalation was raised for the review, and the intent stays frozen until a person decides. {mentions}: decide on the escalation with `/decide <resume|terminate> [reason_code] [reason]`: `resume` starts a new run after G4, `terminate` closes the intent.
intent.status.run_terminated: **{code}**: the escalation of its last run was decided `terminate`. The intent is closed.
intent.status.run_not_started: **{code}**: the agent run could not start (for example the budget is used up, or the run proposal changed). The intent is back at **G4** ({gate_name}), where the platform decides again. {mentions}
intent.status.proposal_ready: **{code}**: the agent run (autonomy L1) ended with a proposal only. The platform stored it as evidence; no code was pushed. The intent is paused at **G4** ({gate_name}) while Person A takes the proposal forward. {mentions}
intent.status.run_returned: **{code}**: the escalation of the failed run was decided `modify` or `roll_back`: the intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). G3 is now HITL at every risk tier. {mentions}: change the plan and submit it again, or approve the same plan again.
intent.status.run_resumed: **{code}**: the escalation of the last run allows a new run. The intent is back at **G4** ({gate_name}). {mentions}
intent.status.budget_warning: **{code}**: the agent run has used {percent} % of its budget limit (warning share `budget.warn_percent`). {mentions}: check the spend. At the stop share (`budget.stop_percent`) the platform stops the run, and G5 raises an escalation.
intent.status.scope_returned: **{code}**: the agent run changed files outside the approved plan (reason code `{reason}`). G5 failed, and the intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). {mentions}: submit a **new** plan. G3 is now HITL at every risk tier, and the plan the run went outside of cannot be approved again. The run's diff is kept as evidence.
intent.status.g5_breach: **{code}**: G5 ({gate_name}) found a breach in the agent run (reason code `{reason}`). The intent is paused, and an escalation was raised. {mentions}: decide on the escalation with `/decide <resume|modify|terminate> [reason_code] [reason]`: `resume` starts a new run after G4 (a budget increase only through the API), `modify` takes the intent back to G3, `terminate` closes it.
intent.status.g5_returned: **{code}**: the escalation of its G5 breach was decided `modify` or `roll_back`: the intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). G3 is now HITL at every risk tier. {mentions}: change the plan, or approve the same plan again. The run's diff is kept as evidence.
intent.status.terminated: **{code}**: the escalation of its G5 breach was decided `terminate`. The intent is closed. The run's diff is kept as evidence.
intent.status.spec_changed: **{code}**: its spec changed. The file at the head of the default branch differs from the spec that was checked, or a new spec was linked. The platform links the new version; the intent now waits at **{gate}** ({gate_name}); it was at {previous_gate}. Approvals of the old spec no longer count. {mentions}: check the new spec at G2.
intent.status.spec_unavailable: **{code}**: its spec cannot be read at the head of the default branch (the file was removed or renamed, is not a file, is larger than 256 KiB, or is not UTF-8 text). The intent waits at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). {mentions}: restore the file, or link a spec with `adlc spec link`.
intent.status.spec_unclear: **{code}**: its spec has no acceptance criteria, so **{gate}** ({gate_name}) cannot pass. The intent waits. {mentions}: add acceptance criteria to the spec (a section such as `## Acceptance criteria` with one list item per criterion), then link it again with `adlc spec link`.
intent.status.plan_changed: **{code}**: a new plan was submitted after G3. The intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}); it was at {previous_gate}. Approvals of the old plan no longer count. {mentions}: check the new plan at G3.
intent.status.plan_resubmit_needed: **{code}**: the plan file `.sdlc/plans/{code}.yaml` at the head of the default branch is no longer the submitted plan (it changed, was removed, or cannot be read). The intent waits at **{gate}** ({gate_name}) and does not move on. {mentions}: submit the plan again with `adlc plan submit {code}`. Whoever submits a plan never approves it at G3.
intent.status.pr_opened: **{code}**: the platform pushed the agent's checked changes to the agent branch and opened a pull request. The intent waits at **{gate}** ({gate_name}) for CI. {mentions}
intent.status.g6_publish_stopped: **{code}**: the platform could not push the agent's changes or open the pull request (for example the run changed nothing, or someone else changed the agent branch). The intent is paused at **{gate}** ({gate_name}), and a `technical` escalation was raised. {mentions}: decide on the escalation with `/decide <resume|modify|terminate> [reason_code] [reason]`: `resume` starts a new run after G4 (restore or delete a changed agent branch first), `modify` takes the intent back to G3, `terminate` closes it.
intent.status.g6_returned: **{code}**: the escalation at G6 was decided `modify` or `roll_back`: the intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). G3 is now HITL at every risk tier. {mentions}: change the plan, or approve the same plan again.
intent.status.g6_terminated: **{code}**: the escalation at G6 was decided `terminate`. The intent is closed. The run's diff is kept as evidence; close the pull request if one is open.
pr.title: {code}: changes of the agent run {run_short}
pr.body:
## Description

Changes made by the platform's agent for intent **{code}**, run `{run_id}`. The platform checked them at gate G5 (file scope against the approved plan, agent instruction files, budget) before it pushed them.

## Links

- Task / intent: {code}{issue}
- Run ID: `{run_id}`
- Agent: `{agent}` version `{agent_version}`, model `{model}`, autonomy {autonomy}
- Approved plan: SHA-256 `{plan_sha256}`
- Diff checked at G5: SHA-256 `{diff_sha256}`
- Related design doc: none (agent change)

## AI disclosure

- [ ] No AI used
- [ ] AI wrote **part** of this change (list below)
- [x] AI wrote **most / all** of this change

Human review (ticked **only by the reviewer**, when approving — never by the author or the AI):

- [ ] A human reviewed every file — reviewer:

AI tools used: agent `{agent}` (OpenHands) through the SDLC platform

Parts written by AI: every file in this pull request.

## Verification

- [ ] Tests cover **every** acceptance criterion (AC) of the task
- [ ] Lint, type check and tests pass in CI (gate G6)
- [x] Only files in the approved plan were changed (checked by the platform at G5)
- [ ] No secrets, no real client data
- [ ] Related docs updated if user-visible behaviour changed

Changes outside the plan: none (G5 refuses them).

## Points for the reviewer

The agent wrote every file: review all of them. The platform filled this description from codes only. Decide the gates with comments on the intent's issue.

intent.status.ci_retry: **{code}**: CI failed on the pull request of the agent run (reason code `{reason}`). The intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}): the platform starts a new run on top of the pushed commit, and the agent is told to fix the failing checks. {mentions}
intent.status.ci_returned: **{code}**: CI failed again and no retry is left (configuration `run.g6_ci_retries`). The intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}), which is now HITL at every risk tier. {mentions}: check the plan (and the spec); approve the same plan again or submit a changed one. The pull request stays open.
intent.status.g6_decision: **{code}**: CI passed on the pull request. Gate **{gate}** ({gate_name}) needs a person's decision (the risk tier, a security finding at the configured severity, or findings the platform cannot read). {mentions}: review the checks and the findings, then decide with `/approve G6`, `/reject G6 <reason>` or `/request-changes G6 <reason>`.
intent.status.g6_escalated: **{code}**: G6 ({gate_name}) stopped (a CI timeout, the pull request was closed, merged or changed by someone else, or a critical security finding). The intent is paused, and an escalation was raised. {mentions}: decide on the escalation with `/decide <resume|modify|terminate> [reason_code] [reason]`.
intent.status.g6_resumed: **{code}**: the escalation at G6 was decided, or the pull request changed. The intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}), where the platform reads CI again. {mentions}
intent.status.g7_review_needed: **{code}**: the pull request of the agent run waits for review at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). {mentions}: review the pull request on GitHub and submit a review: **Approve**, or **Request changes**. Only reviews of the latest commit count; the producers never count: the author of the intent, the people who allowed the runs, the plan submitters and the commit authors. Reject with `/reject G7 <reason>`.
intent.status.g7_changes_requested: **{code}**: {deciders} requested changes at **{previous_gate}** (reason code `{reason}`). The intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}): the platform starts a new run on top of the pushed commit, and the agent gets the feedback of that review or comment. The approvals of the pushed commit no longer count. {mentions}
intent.status.g7_merge_ready: **{code}**: the approvals of the pull request at **{gate}** ({gate_name}) are complete. {mentions}: merge the pull request on GitHub. The platform never merges; it moves on to G8 when the approved commit is merged.
intent.status.g7_escalated: **{code}**: G7 ({gate_name}) stopped: the pull request was closed, changed by someone other than the platform, or merged before its approvals were complete (or by an account that may not merge it). The intent is paused, and an escalation was raised. {mentions}: decide on the escalation with `/decide <resume|modify|roll-back|terminate> [reason_code] [reason]`.
intent.status.g7_returned: **{code}**: G7 sent the intent back to **{gate}** ({gate_name}) (a rejection, reason code `{reason}`, or a `modify` or `roll_back` decision). G3 is now HITL at every risk tier. {mentions}: change the plan, or approve the same plan again. The pull request stays open; the next run continues from its last commit.
intent.status.g7_resumed: **{code}**: the escalation at G7 was decided, or the pull request changed. The intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}), where the platform reads the pull request again. {mentions}
intent.status.g7_terminated: **{code}**: the escalation at G7 was decided `terminate`. The intent is closed. Close the pull request if it is still open; revert a merged change on the default branch yourself.
intent.status.merged: **{code}**: the approved pull request was merged. G7 passed, and the intent now waits at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). {mentions}
intent.status.g8_review_needed: **{code}** waits for the release approval at **{gate}** ({gate_name}). The platform built the Evidence Pack (`adlc evidence show {code}`); the approval is bound to its release hash. {mentions}: check the pack and the release record (template T14), then approve with `/approve G8`, or reject with `/reject G8 <reason>`. The author of the intent, the people who allowed its runs and the plan submitters never approve.{client_note}
intent.status.g8_client_note: **Client disclosure:** this project uses the client's own disclosure format. The PM/BrSE writes the note from the project AI record ({record_ref}); approving G8 confirms that the client's note is ready.
intent.status.g8_changes_requested: **{code}**: {deciders} requested changes at **{gate}** (reason code `{reason}`). The change is already merged: a fix needs a new intent. The intent stays at G8; approvals given before this request no longer count. {mentions}
intent.status.g8_refused: **{code}**: **{gate}** ({gate_name}) cannot pass: the Evidence Pack has no client AI disclosure note (reason code `{reason}`: the project AI record is missing). {mentions}: save the project AI record (`adlc ai-record set`); G8 checks again.
intent.status.g8_escalated: **{code}**: G8 ({gate_name}) stopped: a stored evidence file failed its hash check while the release pack was built (a possible tampering). The intent is paused, and a `security` escalation was raised. {mentions}: decide on the escalation with `/decide <resume|terminate> [reason_code] [reason]`.
intent.status.g8_resumed: **{code}**: the escalation at G8 was decided `resume`. The intent is back at **{gate}** ({gate_name}); the platform builds the Evidence Pack again. {mentions}
intent.status.g8_terminated: **{code}**: the escalation at G8 was decided `terminate`. The intent is closed without a release; the pack is not sealed.
intent.status.released: **{code}**: G8 passed ({deciders} approved the release). The platform sealed the Evidence Pack, and the intent is closed (`done`).

cli.evidence.usage:
Usage (build: the roles in access.evidence_build_roles, by default Person A, Person B, PM / BrSE, governance and admin; read: access.evidence_read_roles, the same and the second approver; tenant admins always; never viewer):
  adlc evidence build <INT-…> [--json]
  adlc evidence list <INT-…> [--json]
  adlc evidence show <INT-…> [--version <n>] [--json]
  adlc evidence export <INT-…> [--version <n>] [--manifest] [--output <file>]
  adlc evidence proposal <INT-…> [--run <run ID>] --output <file> [--force] [--json]
  build makes a new version only when the recorded data changed. export prints the Markdown file (or the JSON manifest with --manifest) after checking its SHA-256; --output saves it to a new file (mode 600, never overwritten). Default version: the latest. proposal saves the patch of a High-risk (L1) run (default: the latest) after checking its SHA-256: client code, mode 600, never printed; --force replaces an existing file.

trial.usage:
Usage (developer machine only, throw-away keys; the trial guide is TRIAL.md):
  pnpm trial:up --settings <file outside the repository> [--passphrase-stdin]
  pnpm trial:start [--passphrase-stdin]
  pnpm trial:down [--wipe] [--settings <file>] [--yes]
trial:up asks for a passphrase that protects the trial stack's key file; trial:start asks for it again after a reboot or trial:down. --passphrase-stdin reads it from the first line of standard input instead (never give it as an argument). trial:down stops the trial stack. --wipe also removes its volumes, its env file, its TLS folder, its key file and, with --settings, the credentials files of Person A and Person B; it asks you to type the project name first (--yes skips the question).
trial.settings.unreadable: Cannot read the settings file {path}. Copy platform/deploy/trial/trial-settings.example.yaml to a place outside the repository and fill it in.
trial.settings.invalid: The settings file {path} has a missing or wrong value at {field}. See platform/deploy/trial/trial-settings.example.yaml.
trial.refused.production: Refused: NODE_ENV is production. pnpm trial:up is for a developer machine only; on a server follow platform/deploy/README.md, Fresh deployment.
trial.refused.env_exists: Refused: {path} exists. trial:up never overwrites a settings file of another stack. If it is an earlier trial stack, remove it with pnpm trial:down --wipe.
trial.refused.volumes_exist: Refused: {count} Docker volume(s) of a platform stack exist, for example {first}. trial:up never removes them. An earlier trial stack: pnpm trial:down --wipe. A development stack (sdlc_*): use another machine, or stop here.
trial.refused.volumes_unknown: Docker could not list its volumes, so trial:up cannot check that no other stack would be touched. Check `docker volume ls`, then try again.
trial.refused.no_docker: Refused: Docker does not answer. Start Docker Desktop or the Docker Engine, then run trial:up again.
trial.refused.compose_old: Refused: Docker Compose {version} is too old; version 2.24 or later is needed.
trial.refused.openssl: Refused: `openssl` is {version}; OpenSSL 3 or later is needed (on macOS /usr/bin/openssl is LibreSSL: brew install openssl@3, then put it first on the PATH; platform/deploy/README.md, Requirements).
trial.refused.docker_memory: Refused: Docker has {have} GiB of memory; the trial stack needs at least {need} GiB. On Docker Desktop: Settings, Resources, Memory.
trial.refused.host_memory: Refused: this machine has {have} GiB of memory; the trial with the model {model} needs at least {need} GiB (TRIAL.md section 1).
trial.refused.ollama_unreachable: Refused: Ollama does not answer at the address of the settings file. Start Ollama on this machine first.
trial.refused.ollama_model_missing: Refused: Ollama does not have the model {tag}. Run: ollama pull {tag} (a local tag, never a :cloud model).
trial.refused.file_mode: Refused: {path} holds a secret but others can read it (mode {mode}). Run: chmod 600 {path}
trial.refused.fork_instructions: Refused: the clone {path} has no AGENTS.md on its main branch. Clone your fork of the sample repository there and fetch main.
trial.refused.credentials_exist: Refused: {path} exists. trial:up never overwrites a saved login. Log out first (adlc logout with that config folder) or choose another config_home.
trial.throwaway_warning: Trial stack on this machine, with THROW-AWAY keys: it can never hold client data. The two OpenBao key shares that unseal it are kept in a key file next to its env file, encrypted with a passphrase you choose, so pnpm trial:start can start it again after a reboot or pnpm trial:down. It takes 20 to 40 minutes.
trial.step.2: Step 2 of 13: the settings file (Compose project of the trial).
trial.step.3: Step 3 of 13: OpenBao, initialised and unsealed with throw-away keys.
trial.step.4: Step 4 of 13: the shared secrets (GitHub App key, gateway keys, the model).
trial.step.5: Step 5 of 13: the credentials of every process; then the root token is revoked.
trial.step.7: Step 7 of 13: starting the platform (core, models, platform, sandbox); this can take 15 minutes the first time.
trial.step.8: Step 8 of 13: the tenant, with Person A as its first admin.
trial.step.9: Step 9 of 13: the project, Person A and Person B with their GitHub accounts and roles, their logins.
trial.step.10: Step 10 of 13: the sandbox image (built once, about 10 minutes).
trial.step.11: Step 11 of 13: the agent, approved by Person A (owner) and Person B.
trial.step.12: Step 12 of 13: the trial configuration (design/M-E-TRIAL-PLAN.md section 6).
trial.step.13: Step 13 of 13: the project AI record (data class internal: the project is fictional).
trial.done:
The trial stack is ready (Compose project {compose_project}, API {api_url}, project {project}, model {model}).
  Person A is logged in: {person_a}. Use pnpm adlc as usual.
  Person B is logged in: {person_b}. Run Person B's commands as: XDG_CONFIG_HOME={config_b} pnpm adlc …
  Next: TRIAL.md section 5, task T01 (platform/USER-GUIDE.md takes it from G1 to G8).
  Stop the stack: pnpm trial:down. After a reboot or trial:down: pnpm trial:start (your passphrase). Remove it: pnpm trial:down --wipe --settings <file>.
trial.step_failed: trial:up stopped at: {step}. The end of its output follows (secrets removed).
trial.unexpected: trial:up stopped with an unexpected error ({kind}). Its text is not shown, because it may contain a secret.
trial.failed_hint: This stack cannot be completed. Remove it with pnpm trial:down --wipe --settings <file> (this also removes its key file), fix the cause, and run pnpm trial:up again.
trial.down.refused.no_env: Nothing to do: {path} does not exist.
trial.down.refused.not_trial: Refused: {path} belongs to another Compose project, not the trial stack {project}. trial:down acts only on the trial stack.
trial.down.confirm: This removes every volume of the Compose project {project} (all trial data). Type the project name to go on:
trial.down.failed: docker compose down failed. Its last lines follow.
trial.down.stopped: The trial stack {project} is stopped. OpenBao is sealed now; start the stack again with pnpm trial:start (it asks for your passphrase).
trial.down.wiped: The trial stack {project} is removed: its volumes, env file, TLS folder, key file and (with --settings) the trial logins.
trial.down.kept_login: Kept {path}: it holds a login to another platform, not to this trial stack.
trial.down.stopped_no_key_file: The trial stack {project} is stopped. It has no key file (it was set up before trial:start existed), so OpenBao cannot be unsealed again: pnpm trial:down --wipe, then pnpm trial:up. The trial's intents (fictional data) are lost.
trial.passphrase.explain: Choose a passphrase (at least 12 characters) for the trial stack's key file. You need it with pnpm trial:start after a reboot or pnpm trial:down. If you forget it, the stack cannot be started again: its data is fictional, so then remove it (pnpm trial:down --wipe) and run pnpm trial:up again.
trial.passphrase.prompt_new: New passphrase for the trial stack (hidden):
trial.passphrase.too_short: The passphrase is too short: at least {min} characters.
trial.passphrase.too_long: The passphrase is too long: at most 1024 characters.
trial.passphrase.aborted: No passphrase given: nothing was changed.
trial.passphrase.needs_tty: Refused: no terminal to ask the passphrase. Run it in a terminal, or give the passphrase on the first line of standard input with --passphrase-stdin (never as an argument or an environment variable).
trial.keys.saved: The key shares are saved, encrypted with your passphrase, in {path} (mode 600). Only pnpm trial:start reads it. Never copy it to a server.
trial.refused.key_file_exists: Refused: {path} exists. trial:up never overwrites a key file. If it belongs to an earlier trial stack, remove that stack with pnpm trial:down --wipe.
trial.refused.key_file_not_ignored: Refused: Git does not ignore {path}, so the key file could be committed. Use a checkout whose .gitignore lists trial-openbao-keys.age.
trial.start.refused.production: Refused: NODE_ENV is production. pnpm trial:start is for a trial stack on a developer machine only; a server keeps the key-holder rules (runbook T11 section 4).
trial.start.refused.no_env: Nothing to start: {path} does not exist. Set up a trial stack with pnpm trial:up.
trial.start.refused.not_trial: Refused: {path} belongs to another Compose project, not the trial stack {project}. trial:start acts only on the trial stack; a server keeps the key-holder rules (runbook T11 section 4).
trial.start.error.not_trial_container: Refused: the openbao container does not belong to the trial stack {project}. Nothing was unsealed.
trial.start.error.not_initialised: OpenBao of the trial stack {project} is not initialised: the stack is broken. Remove it with pnpm trial:down --wipe, then run pnpm trial:up again.
trial.start.error.no_key_file: OpenBao is sealed and {path} does not exist: this trial stack was set up before trial:start existed (or its key file was deleted), so it cannot be unsealed. Remove it with pnpm trial:down --wipe and run pnpm trial:up again; the trial's intents (fictional data) are lost.
trial.start.error.key_file_mode: Refused: others can read {path}. Run: chmod 600 {path}
trial.start.error.key_file_invalid: Refused: {path} is not a key file of trial:up. Nothing was unsealed.
trial.start.error.key_file_project: Refused: {path} belongs to another Compose project, not {project}. Nothing was unsealed.
trial.start.error.wrong_passphrase: Wrong passphrase: nothing was unsealed. Run pnpm trial:start again. If you forgot the passphrase, the stack cannot be started again: its data is fictional, so remove it with pnpm trial:down --wipe and run pnpm trial:up again.
trial.start.ageing: This trial stack is {days} days old. Its processes' credentials end after {max} days and a trial stack cannot renew them: plan to set it up again soon (pnpm trial:down --wipe, then pnpm trial:up).
trial.start.expired: This trial stack is {days} days old: its processes' credentials ended after {max} days, so the platform will not start. Remove it with pnpm trial:down --wipe and run pnpm trial:up again.
trial.start.no_key_file_warning: OpenBao is unsealed, but this trial stack has no key file: after the next reboot or trial:down it cannot be unsealed again.
trial.start.step.openbao: Starting OpenBao and the database of the trial stack.
trial.start.step.unseal: Unsealing OpenBao with the key file.
trial.start.step.migrate: Applying the database migrations (nothing to do when they are current).
trial.start.step.up: Starting the platform (core, models, platform, sandbox); this can take a few minutes.
trial.start.step_failed: trial:start stopped at: {step}. The end of its output follows (secrets removed).
trial.start.done: The trial stack {project} is unsealed and running (API {api_url}). Person A and Person B use their saved logins as before.
trial.start.done_already: OpenBao of the trial stack {project} was already unsealed; the platform is running (API {api_url}).
server_setup.usage: Usage: pnpm server:setup --settings <file outside the repository>. It runs platform/deploy/README.md "Fresh deployment" steps 2 to 7 on a server (runbook T11 §3.2).
server_setup.refused.stdout_not_terminal: server:setup shows key shares: run it in a terminal, never with its output redirected or piped. Nothing was changed.
server_setup.refused.stdin_not_terminal: server:setup asks for key shares and tokens at hidden prompts: run it in a terminal, never with its input redirected or piped. Nothing was changed.
server_setup.refused.litellm_keys_in_env: {path} sets LITELLM_MASTER_KEY or LITELLM_SALT_KEY. On a server both stay empty: LiteLLM gets its keys from OpenBao (runbook T11 §5d). Empty them, then start again.
server_setup.refused.trial_project: The env file belongs to a trial stack ({project}). server:setup is for a server; on a developer machine use pnpm trial:up.
server_setup.refused.pgp_key_invalid: The PGP key file of {holder} is not a PGP public key (make it with: gpg --export --armor <key>). OpenBao was not initialised.
server_setup.refused.no_share: No key share was given. Start again when the key holders are ready.
server_setup.refused.secret_file_mode: {path} can be read by other users. A secret file must be readable by its owner only: chmod 600 {path}, then start again.
server_setup.refused.env_conflict: {path} already sets {key} to another value than the settings file. The command never overwrites it: make the two agree (README "Team access", "The runner on its own Docker Engine"), then start again. Nothing was changed.
server_setup.admin.not_revoked: OpenBao did not confirm that the admin token is revoked. It stops working within 1 hour; record it in the operations log (runbook T11 §5.1).
server_setup.share.stop_warning: Stop now? {shown} of {total} key shares are handed out. The others exist only in this command: if it stops, OpenBao must be initialised again on wiped volumes.
server_setup.share.stop_confirm: Press Enter to go on (this holder's share is shown again), or Ctrl-C again to stop.
server_setup.settings.invalid: The settings file {path}: the field {field} is missing or not valid (example: platform/deploy/server-setup/server-settings.example.yaml).
server_setup.settings.inside_repo: The settings file {path} is inside the repository. Keep it outside, next to the secret files it names.
server_setup.resume: The last run stopped at step {step} ({reason}, {at}). The steps already done are skipped.
server_setup.resume.root_not_revoked: The last run stopped before it could revoke its root token (OpenBao was sealed or not reachable). This run revokes it, by its accessor, before it runs configure.
server_setup.resume.root_revoked: Revoked the root tokens of earlier runs: {count}.
server_setup.step.5: Step 5: the credentials of every process.
server_setup.tls.replace_first: Step 2 is done: {path} is new, with a throw-away certificate for OpenBao. On the server, replace it now with the company CA's certificate (runbook T11 §3c: pnpm openbao:tls ca <offline folder>, then pnpm openbao:tls server <offline folder>). Then run pnpm server:setup again: it goes on with step 3.
server_setup.init.pgp: OpenBao is initialised now with one key share per key holder ({holders}). Each share is encrypted with its holder's PGP key: this command never sees a share in clear.
server_setup.init.plain: OpenBao is initialised now with one key share per key holder ({holders}). The shares are shown one at a time, to one holder at a time. Nothing is written to a file.
server_setup.init.ready: Are all key holders here, nobody else can see the screen, and the operations log is open? Do not stop the command until every holder has their share. Press Enter to initialise OpenBao (Ctrl-C stops).
server_setup.share.call: Share {n} of {total} is for {holder}. Only {holder} looks at the screen now. Press Enter to show it.
server_setup.share.plain: {holder}, this is your key share ({n} of {total}). Copy it into your password manager and onto paper for your envelope:
server_setup.share.pgp: {holder}, this is your key share ({n} of {total}), encrypted with your PGP key. Copy it into your password manager and onto paper. To read it: echo '<share>' | base64 -d | gpg -dq
server_setup.share.copied: {holder}: press Enter when your copy is done. The screen and its scroll-back are cleared.
server_setup.share.all_copied: All {total} key shares are handed out. None is stored anywhere.
server_setup.share.prompt: Key share {n} of {threshold} (hidden; each key holder types their own share):
server_setup.unseal.explain: Unseal: {threshold} key holders type their share at the hidden prompt.
server_setup.admin.needs_root: configure needs a root token: two key holders type their shares. configure revokes the root token at once and gives the admin token for the next steps.
server_setup.langfuse.explain: Langfuse runs at {url}. Create the worker's own project key there (runbook T11 §5m), then type it below.
server_setup.langfuse.public_key: The worker's Langfuse public key (pk-lf-..., hidden):
server_setup.langfuse.secret_key: The worker's Langfuse secret key (sk-lf-..., hidden):
server_setup.env.keys: Written to the env file from the settings: {keys}.
server_setup.runner_link.configure_again: SDLC_RUNNER_SOURCE_CIDR is new and OpenBao is already configured: configure runs again so the AppRole runner accepts the runner host (two key holders type their shares).
server_setup.access.ready: Team access: people open {url}/dashboard/ and sign in with adlc login --api-url {url} (README "Team access"). Check it from another machine of the LAN.
server_setup.runner_link.next: The runner runs on its own Engine. On the runner host, as the runner's user, start it now: platform/deploy/scripts/runner-host.sh up{profiles} (README "The runner on its own Docker Engine" step 7). Then pnpm doctor shows runner.engine ok.
server_setup.step.8: Step 8: the tenant and its first admin.
server_setup.step.9: Steps 9 to 12: the project, its team, the agent and the project configuration, from the project file.
server_setup.refused.project_file: {path} is not a project file that this command can read (format 1, with project.slug and team; deploy/project.example.yaml). Nothing was changed in steps 8 to 13.
server_setup.refused.sandbox_image_confl: {path} sets config.sandbox.image to another image than sandbox_image in the settings file. Keep one of them, then start again.
server_setup.refused.no_person_a: {path} names no team member with the role person_a. The project AI record is written on behalf of Person A: add Person A, then start again.
server_setup.token.show: This is the API token of {email}, the first tenant admin. It is shown once. Copy it into your password manager now:
server_setup.token.copied: Press Enter when your copy is done. The screen and its scroll-back are cleared, then the command logs you in with it.
server_setup.tenant.ready: Tenant {tenant}: {email} is its first admin and is logged in on this server.
server_setup.apply.nothing: Project {project}: the platform already matches the project file. Nothing to change.
server_setup.apply.changes: Project {project}: {count} changes to make. The platform matches people by the numeric GitHub ID only: check each ID above.
server_setup.apply.confirm: Press Enter if every GitHub ID is right (Ctrl-C stops, nothing is changed).
server_setup.ai_record.done: The project AI record of {project} matches the settings file (written on behalf of {email}, Person A).
server_setup.ai_record.by_hand: No ai_record in the settings file: Person A writes the project AI record of {project} (README "Fresh deployment" step 13).
server_setup.team.left: These commands stay with people. The command never runs them for you:
server_setup.team.first_intent: {email} (Person A): the first intent, README "Fresh deployment" step 14: adlc intent create --project {project} --title "<title>" --risk low --data-class internal
server_setup.team.by_hand: No tenant, admin, project_file and sandbox_image in the settings file: README "Fresh deployment" steps 8 to 14 stay by hand.
server_setup.done: The setup is done and the admin token is revoked. The API is at {api_url}.
server_setup.done_doctor_failed: The setup ran, but doctor found a problem (above). Fix it with the README "Troubleshooting" table, then run pnpm doctor.
server_setup.failed: Step {step} failed at: {what}. See {section}. The end of its output follows (secrets removed). Fix the cause, then run pnpm server:setup again: it skips what is done.
server_setup.stopped: No root token is left valid. Run pnpm server:setup again to go on.
server_setup.stopped_root_not_revoked: The root token of this run could not be revoked (OpenBao was sealed or not reachable). The next pnpm server:setup revokes it before configure; until then OpenBao stays sealed or unconfigured. Record it in the operations log.
server_setup.unexpected: server:setup stopped with an unexpected error ({kind}). Nothing secret is shown.
github_app.usage:
Usage (run it yourself, in a terminal, never through a chat tool):
  pnpm github-app:create --out <key file outside the repository> [--org <organization>] [--name <app name>] [--callback-url <url>]… [--force]
It creates the platform's GitHub App from platform/deploy/github-app/manifest.json, saves its private key to --out and its client secret to <--out>.client-secret (both mode 600). --org creates it in an organization you administer instead of your own account; --name defaults to sdlc-<random>; --callback-url (repeat it, at most 10) lists the dashboard's sign-in callbacks, default http://localhost:8090/v1/auth/github/callback; --force replaces existing files.
github_app.refused.callback_url: Refused: --callback-url must be https://<host>/v1/auth/github/callback, or http://localhost:<port>/v1/auth/github/callback (at most 10).
github_app.refused.org: Refused: --org must be a GitHub organization login (letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 39 characters).
github_app.refused.name: Refused: --name must be 1 to 34 characters: letters, digits, spaces, dots, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
github_app.refused.in_repo: Refused: {path} is inside the repository. Keep the private key in a file outside every repository, for example ~/secrets/sdlc-app.private-key.pem.
github_app.refused.no_folder: Refused: the folder of {path} does not exist. Create it first (mkdir -p, then chmod 700).
github_app.refused.exists: Refused: {path} exists. Choose another file, or add --force to replace it.
github_app.refused.not_a_file: Refused: {path} is not a regular file (a link, a folder or a device). Choose another file.
github_app.open:
Open this page in your browser, signed in to GitHub, and press the button: {url}
GitHub then shows the new App "{name}" with the platform's permissions; confirm with "Create GitHub App". The browser comes back to this computer, and this command saves the key.
github_app.paste_prompt: If the browser shows an error at 127.0.0.1 after GitHub, copy its whole address and paste it here (hidden), then press Enter:
github_app.paste_refused: That is not the address of this run (wrong or missing state) nor a code. Paste the whole address from the browser's address bar.
github_app.manifest_invalid: The manifest {path} is missing or loosens the App's settings (webhook on, public, events, an unknown permission level). Restore it from the repository.
github_app.timeout: No answer from GitHub within 15 minutes. Nothing was saved. Run the command again; if an App was created on GitHub meanwhile, delete it there first (Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps).
github_app.cancelled: Cancelled. Nothing was saved. If an App was created on GitHub meanwhile, delete it there (Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps).
github_app.conversion.unreachable: Cannot reach the GitHub API to finish the App. Nothing was saved. The code from GitHub works for one hour and once only: run the command again, or delete the App on GitHub and create it by hand (platform/deploy/README.md, Create the GitHub App, option B).
github_app.conversion.refused: GitHub refused the code (HTTP {status}): it was used already or is older than one hour. Nothing was saved. Delete the App on GitHub if it exists, and run the command again.
github_app.conversion.bad_response: GitHub's answer did not hold the expected App fields. Nothing was saved. Check the App on GitHub (Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps); generate a private key there by hand, or delete the App and run the command again.
github_app.write_failed: The App {slug} (App ID {id}) exists on GitHub, but its private key could not be saved. On GitHub, open the App, generate a new private key by hand and keep it outside the repository (chmod 600).
github_app.secret_write_failed: The App {slug} (App ID {id}) exists on GitHub and its private key is saved in {path}, but its client secret could not be saved. You need it only for the dashboard's GitHub sign-in: on GitHub, open the App, generate a new client secret and store it with pnpm openbao:bootstrap api-github-oauth-credentials (runbook T11 section 5n).
github_app.created:
The GitHub App is created.
  App ID:             {id}
  Client ID:          {client_id} (not a secret)
  Key file:           {path} (mode 600; never paste it anywhere)
  Client secret file: {secret_path} (mode 600; never paste it anywhere)
  Sign-in callbacks:  {callbacks}
Next:
  1. Install it on your repository only ("Only select repositories"): {install_url}
  2. The community trial: put the client ID and the key file in your trial settings file (github_app.client_id, github_app.private_key_file; TRIAL.md section 3.2).
     A deployment: store the client ID and the key in OpenBao at kv/shared/github-app (runbook T11 section 5b).
  3. Dashboard sign-in with GitHub (optional): store the client secret with pnpm openbao:bootstrap api-github-oauth-credentials < {secret_path} (runbook T11 section 5n), then delete the file.
The webhook secret GitHub also returned was not kept: the platform uses no webhook.
github_app.page.title: Create the platform's GitHub App
github_app.page.intro: The button sends the App's settings (its permissions, no webhook, only your account) to GitHub. GitHub asks you to confirm before it creates anything.
github_app.page.button: Create the GitHub App on GitHub
github_app.page.done: Done. Go back to the terminal.
github_app.page.refused: Refused: this answer does not belong to this run. Go back to the terminal.
doctor.usage:
Usage: pnpm doctor [--env <file>] [--json]

cli.client.usage:
Usage (tenant admins; through the API; handbook Ch.19 §19.8c):
  adlc client request-data-deletion [--basis <code>] [--json]
  adlc client cancel-data-deletion [--json]
  adlc client status [--json]
request starts a deletion (tenant stays active until an operator approves). cancel aborts an open request or an approved deletion still in the grace period. Default --basis: contract_offboarding. Approval: adlc ops client-data-deletion approve.
cli.client.requested: Deletion requested for tenant {tenant}: phase {phase}, status {status}, grace {grace} days.
cli.client.cancelled: Deletion cancelled for tenant {tenant}: phase {phase}, status {status}.
cli.ops.client_data.usage:
Usage (on the server, SDLC_DB_URL as platform_app; two-person rule; handbook Ch.19 §19.8d):
  adlc ops client-data-deletion approve --tenant <slug> --operator <user-uuid> [--json]
  adlc ops client-data-deletion list [--json]
  adlc ops client-data-deletion status --tenant <slug> [--json]
approve refuses when --operator is the requester. After approve the tenant is pending_deletion; the worker purges after SDLC_CLIENT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS (default 14).
